summary: The note argues that urban parks and gardens are economic assets that raise property values and tax revenue, cut infrastructure and energy costs, create jobs, improve health, and reduce crime. It cites studies and city examples from 2023-2024, including Minneapolis, New York City, Detroit and Charlotte. It also notes funding and maintenance challenges and calls for sustained investment, including public-private partnerships.
one_line: Investing in urban parks and gardens yields economic returns through higher property values, cost savings, jobs, better health and lower crime.
key_facts: The Urban Land Institute study of September 15, 2023 found well-maintained parks and gardens can increase tax revenues, save cities infrastructure costs, and create jobs.
An initiative launched in Minneapolis on October 3, 2023 showed property values rose by 15% within a 500-foot radius of newly developed green spaces.
The Department of Environmental Protection in New York City reported on September 30, 2023 that green infrastructure initiatives saved the city over $200 million in water management costs.
The "Green Belt Festival" held in Charlotte on November 7, 2023 attracted thousands of visitors and boosted the local economy through tourism-related spending.
The "Green Spine" project in Detroit, starting late 2023, is a linear park that transformed a derelict industrial area into a place for new businesses and housing.
A CDC health impact assessment of February 12, 2024 found regular access to green spaces lowers healthcare costs by reducing diseases associated with sedentary lifestyles.
The CDC report said children with access to parks tend to have lower obesity rates and better overall health.
A sociological study led by Dr. Laura Henderson on April 19, 2024 found neighborhoods with quality parks reported stronger community bonds and lower crime rates.
Professor Emily Nguyen said urban greenery cools the air and reduces air conditioning needs, helping municipalities save on electricity bills and emissions.
Philadelphia's "Green City, Clean Waters" initiative shows public-private partnerships and community involvement can overcome funding and maintenance challenges.
A Seattle scheme implemented on January 20, 2024 offers park maintenance and horticulture job training, particularly for youth and marginalized communities.
A park-based event was inaugurated in Dallas on December 5, 2023, an example of food markets, concerts and festivals creating business opportunities and jobs.
